correctness.rationale: PASS: From [H,H]=kz a Lie homomorphism has F(z)=cz and F(v)=Av+ell(v)z. A^T J A=cJ, A^2=A, c^2=c and ell A+c ell=ell follow without dividing by two, so characteristic two is included. The c=1 branch is identity because A is invertible idempotent and ell=0. On c=0, im A is isotropic, A a projection along a complement, and ell descends to a functional of im A. Conversely these choices give all proper retractions. The split idempotent decomposition makes rank locally constant on the functor, so its rank strata are open-closed; complement+functional parameters form a Zariski-locally trivial affine bundle over the smooth irreducible isotropic Grassmannian. Its dimension r(2n-r)-r(r-1)/2 +r(2n-r+1) equals (8nr-5r^2+3r)/2. Isotropic frame choices divided by GL(r,q) give the stated q-Gaussian product. The finite difference d(r)-d(r-1)=4n-5r+4 proves the maximal-rank transition. Independently enumerated 3D Heisenberg projections over F2/F3 (rank profiles 1,12,1 and 1,36,1) and all 65536 4x4 binary A with admissible functionals (proper counts 1,240,960). Finite samples do not establish general scheme geometry; the displayed argument does.
